How to do itKettlebell Swing

Right: Standing tall, ankles, knees, hips and shoulders in line.

Wrong: Leaning back at the top.

Drive1 s
Swing down1 s
Look closer

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in your glutes and the backs of your thighs.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansYou are lifting with the arms instead of the hips.

    FixDrive with your hips. Keep your arms straight and loose.

  • Usually meansA crush grip can stress them.

    FixGrip firmly, not too tightly: an easy hook grip.

  • Usually meansYour form may be breaking down.

    FixStop or reset your form.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Feet about shoulder-width and planted, the bell a foot in front.

  2. 2

    Hinge and grip, palms down side by side, bell tilted toward you.

  3. 3

    Hike it high between your legs, then swing to about chest height.

  4. 4

    Don't hold your breath: out as it rises, in as it falls.

  5. 5

    Keep a full grip. Set the bell on the ground when done.

Risks and when to stop

  • Rounding the lower back strains it.
  • Leaning back at the top puts more pressure on the lower back.
  • A loose grip could let the bell slip or be dropped.

Back pain

How to do itBear Crawl

Hip line

Right
HIPS LEVEL
Wrong
HIPS RAISED

Right: Hips level with the shoulders, back flat.

Wrong: Hips raised above the back.

Palms pressed into the floor, hands under the shoulders, knees under the hips.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Hips riseThe hips rise above the line of the back as the knees lift.
  2. Hips above shouldersThe hips sit higher than the shoulders.
Work15–30 s
Look closer

Grip

Palm pressed into the floor, hand under the shoulder.

Common handling mistakes

  • Hips rise as you crawl

    Fix: Keep hips in line with the back. Bear plank until you can.

  • Back arches

    Fix: Tighten your trunk.

  • Hips sway side to side

    Fix: Take shorter steps.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in your belly and sides, shoulders and front thighs.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt

The core holds the whole body steady.

If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansWith this pain under load, scans often find a wrist problem.

    FixCheck the wrist box below.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Get on hands and knees: hands under shoulders, knees under hips.

  2. 2

    Press palms into the floor, brace, lift knees about 2 inches.

  3. 3

    Move one hand and the opposite foot forward, then switch.

  4. 4

    Keep your back straight and your hips level with your shoulders.

  5. 5

    One drill is 4 steps forward, then 4 steps back.

Risks and when to stop

  • Pain on the back of the wrist in the loaded, bent-back position.
  • An arched back can be painful.

Wrist pain

Can't grip, wrist changed shape, or hand gone numb? Get it checked today.

Tingling, keeps coming back, or no better after two weeks' rest? See a doctor.

General guidance, not medical advice. If something hurts, stop and get it checked.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Back roundsThe back rounds instead of staying flat.

Walk 
Look closer

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in your thighs, glutes and calves.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansA rounded back.

    FixHinge at your hips and keep your back flat.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Load the sled. Check the path is flat and clear.

  2. 2

    Stand behind the sled. Hands about halfway down the handles, arms straight.

  3. 3

    Step back and lean forward, head to hips in a straight line.

  4. 4

    Keep arms straight the whole push, shoulders behind your hands.

  5. 5

    Tighten your abs, spine neutral, eyes just ahead of the sled.

Risks and when to stop

  • Pushing with a rounded back is not good for your spine.
  • Bent arms may cause some discomfort in your elbows and shoulders.
  • Hips rising or chest dropping as you tire? Keep the same body angle.

Slam 
Look closer

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in your abs and lats.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansRounding the back as you slam or pick up the ball.

    FixKeep your back flat and hinge from the hips.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Use a soft ball without much bounce.

  2. 2

    Check the space around you is safe.

  3. 3

    Feet about shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent.

  4. 4

    Hold the ball firmly in both hands at chest height.

  5. 5

    Ball overhead, arms straight. Brace, exhale, slam it hard between your feet.

Risks and when to stop

  • A bouncy ball can fly back up into your face.
  • Take care not to throw the ball onto your toes.
  • A bouncing ball needs ample space around you.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Steps too longA regular-sized step, too long for a beginner.
WalkControlled
Look closer

Grip

Palm pushed into the handle, thumb wrapped, fingers curled around it. Not in the fingers only.

Common handling mistakes

  • Rushing the walk

    Fix: Don't rush for distance. Turn in small steps, not a sharp pivot.

  • Steps too long

    Fix: Take short, deliberate steps. Steps out of control? End the carry.

  • Shrugging as you tire

    Fix: Keep your shoulders back and down. Posture changing? End the carry.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in your forearms and traps.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansA handle starts slipping.

    FixEnd the carry. Bend your hips and knees, lower the weights beside you, feet clear.

  • Usually meansNot bracing your trunk.

    FixBrace before you lift. Stop if you feel pain.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Clear a level, dry route, with room to set down.

  2. 2

    Stand between the weights, feet about hip-width apart.

  3. 3

    Bend at your hips and knees and grip, thumbs wrapped.

  4. 4

    Breathe in, brace, and stand up without jerking the weights.

  5. 5

    Stand fully tall, arms long at your sides, before your first step.

Risks and when to stop

  • Rushing: one misstep could pull a calf, roll an ankle or twist a knee.
  • Not bracing can wreak havoc on your lower back.
  • Without a good grip, the weights may slip and land on your toe.
